title: Exceptions under tts: OCC UpdateConflict retry with counter guard, try/catch OUTSIDE the transaction
instruction: In the sandbox model (Contoso conventions, EXTENSION_PREFIX=Con; the model Descriptor must list ApplicationSuite in ModuleReferences because CustTable and CustAccount live there), create exactly ONE runnable class ConCustCreditMaxUpdater that updates a CustTable record under optimistic concurrency with the canonical retry-statement pattern. Ground both halves of the contract first: get_knowledge(topic="transactions") for the in-tts catchability matrix (inside an open transaction only an EXPLICITLY named Exception::UpdateConflict or the duplicate-key exception can reach an inner catch; every other exception — and any bare catch — aborts the tts and unwinds to the first catch OUTSIDE the block, so an inner catch is dead code) and get_knowledge(topic="error-handling") for the throw/catch rules. The class has exactly two methods: (1) `public static void setCreditMax(CustAccount _accountNum, AmountMST _newCreditMax)` whose body is the OCC retry shape, in this order: declare `CustTable custTable;` and `int retryCount = 0;` plus a maximum of 5 (a `const int maxRetries = 5;` local is preferred; the bound MUST be 5); then a try/catch whose try block — and nothing outside it — contains the transaction: `ttsbegin;` `select firstonly forupdate custTable where custTable.AccountNum == _accountNum;` (firstonly: AccountNum is the unique key and xppbp raises BPErrorSelectUsingFirstOnly without it — observed at capture) then `if (custTable.RecId) { custTable.CreditMax = _newCreditMax; custTable.update(); }` and `ttscommit;` (the tts pair must be balanced — validator TTS001; record-not-found handling is deliberately out of scope, the guard just skips the update). The method has exactly ONE catch branch and it sits OUTSIDE the tts scope (after ttscommit): `catch (Exception::UpdateConflict)` — no bare catch and no catch inside the ttsbegin/ttscommit block anywhere in the class (validator TTS002 flags such a catch as dead code and any TTS002 finding is a fail). The catch body is the counter-guarded retry, in this order: `retryCount++;` then `if (retryCount >= maxRetries) { throw Exception::UpdateConflictNotRecovered; }` then `retry;` — the visible ++/if guard before the retry statement is exactly what validator TTS003 checks, and UpdateConflictNotRecovered is the correct exhaustion signal precisely because the NotRecovered variants can never be caught inside a transaction. Use the X++ `retry` statement (it jumps back to the start of the try block); a while-loop rewrite without `retry` is NOT acceptable for this case. Do not call ttsabort anywhere — the conflict already aborted the transaction before the catch ran. (2) `public static void main(Args _args)` which makes the class runnable by calling `ConCustCreditMaxUpdater::setCreditMax('US-001', 25000);` (US-001 is a standard Contoso USMF customer). The class must build with zero errors and pass validate_xpp with zero TTS001/TTS002/TTS003 findings. Correctness is judged in the golden X++ source: the try/catch outside the tts block, the single explicit Exception::UpdateConflict catch, the retryCount guard with bound 5 before `retry;`, and the throw of Exception::UpdateConflictNotRecovered on exhaustion — a version that compiles but nests the catch inside the transaction, uses a bare catch, retries without the counter guard, or swallows the exhausted conflict instead of throwing UpdateConflictNotRecovered is a fail.
